newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Latest Venezuelan oilspill 20 barrels - report.
newsitem.headline: Latest Venezuelan oilspill 20 barrels - report.

text.p: An official report on the latest oilspill in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo said it amounted to only 20 barrels of crude oil, contrary to earlier reports indicating higher figures.

The spill occurred on May 27 while the Maltese-flagged Plate Princess tanker was discharging its ballast into the Lake before loading a cargo of crude from the Puerto Miranda terminal, the official report written by the Energy and Mines Ministry said.
Shippers say tankers normally discharge their ballast into the sea before taking on cargo, but in this case, their was a leak from the oil tanks into the segregated ballast area.

Shipping sources in Maracaibo say about 100 barrels of crude oil are spilled into the lake every year from small accidents, but Venezuela has become highly sensitised to oil pollution since a spill of 25,000 barrels in Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on Febraury 28.
Earlier, the Maracaibo Coast Guard said 8,000 tonnes of contaminated water was discharged into the lake and shipping sources said as much as 35 percent of this was oil.
The Plate Princess was detained by the Port Captain and the National Guard, pending an investigation.
The ship was operated by Argentinian company Powtec and chartered by Korea's Daewoo to load 300,000 tonnes of crude destined for two ports in the Caribbean, shippers said.
